statement: For exactly two real values of $x$, the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} x & 3 \\ 2 & x - 5 \end{bmatrix}$ does not have an inverse. What is the positive one of these two values?

choices.misconception: I set the determinant $x^2 - 5x - 6$ equal to zero but factored it as $(x + 6)(x - 1)$, with the signs swapped.
I found the determinant as $x(x - 5) + 6$, adding the cross product instead of subtracting it, so I solved $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$, got 2 and 3, and picked the larger.
I thought a matrix has no inverse when one of its entries is zero, so I set $x - 5 = 0$.

hints: A $2 \times 2$ matrix has no inverse when its determinant is zero.
For $\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$ the determinant is $ad - bc$. Write it for this matrix, set it equal to zero, and solve.
The determinant is $x(x - 5) - 6 = x^2 - 5x - 6$, which factors as $(x - 6)(x + 1)$.

solutions.reliable: The determinant is $x(x - 5) - 3 \cdot 2 = x^2 - 5x - 6$. The matrix has no inverse when this is zero: $(x - 6)(x + 1) = 0$, so $x = 6$ or $x = -1$. The positive value is $6$. Check: at $x = 6$ the matrix is $\begin{bmatrix} 6 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, whose first row is 3 times its second, and its determinant is $6 - 6 = 0$. The idea: a square matrix has an inverse exactly when its determinant is not zero.
